extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, and typesetters working to prepare manuscripts for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and rules for preparing and formatting manuscripts for publication (punctuation, capitalization, typography, citations, tables, figures, indexing, hyphenation, etc.). Intended to standardize editorial and typesetting decisions across books and periodicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of capitals and small caps; rules for use of, 1-49; capitals: how indicated, 257.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers capitalization of proper nouns, principal words in titles, names of organizations, historical epochs, events, government bodies, etc.; includes rules and word-lists (see sections 1–49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations: spacing, punctuation, and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for abbreviations in literary references and elsewhere; no space between elements of some abbreviations; periods after initials and other rules, 52, 103, 123.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes lists of common abbreviations (biblical, apocryphal, technical terms, titles of publications) and rules for spacing and punctuation (e.g., A.M., B.C., A.D.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accents: retention and typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Retention of accents in foreign words incorporated into English, and treatment of monotone/old-style/monotype accents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States when to retain accents in foreign words and limitations (e.g., no italic accents in some cases); also includes type considerations for accents across point sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostrophe: rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of the apostrophe: possessive formation, contractions, omission of figures or letters, and forming plurals of numerals, 163–165.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains use in contractions, possessives, plural of numerals, and marking omitted letters; cross-references possessive guidance and contractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphens: rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphens: number allowable at line ends; rules for use of hyphens, 182–214.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive treatment of compound words, prefixes, suffixes, word division at line-end, hyphenation lists and conventions for compounds (co-, re-, non-, semi-, vice-, ex-, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics: rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and rules for italics; when to use italics for titles, emphasis, foreign words, symbols, and certain names, 58–73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies italics for titles of books, periodicals, manuscripts, emphasis, foreign words, names of genera/species, and when italics need not be used (e.g., lengthy bibliographies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma: rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and illustrations of comma usage, including many clause- and phrase-level rules, 141–162.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers comma use with conjunctions, adjectives, appositives, adverbial clauses, parenthetical clauses, numbers, thousands separators, and exceptions (e.g., omission between adjectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Colon: rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and illustrations of use of colon; detailed rules 131–136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after salutatory phrases, to introduce statements/extracts/lists, to separate chapter and verse, to separate volume and page, and to emphasize close connections between clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes: definition and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition, sizes, and rules for use of dashes (em, en) including many syntactic roles, 166–175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains em dash for pauses/omissions and en dash for ranges; uses include emphasis, connecting numbers, indicating breaks/transitions, preceding summarizing clauses, and other punctuation functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses: rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of ellipses to indicate omissions and relation to quotations, 180–181; treated as part of quotation, 88, 181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how ellipses indicate omissions in quotations and punctuation conventions for treating ellipses as part of quoted matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and quotations: reduction and punctuation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for citations from different authors, passages in author's own words, reduction of citations, and punctuation of quotations, 74–87, 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on handling consecutive citations, short quotations, punctuation around citations, and reduction/abbreviation conventions in bibliographies and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals: usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for figures vs. spelled-out numbers, treatment of consecutive numbers, grouped numbers, round numbers, and thousands separators, 94–98, 159, 173.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when to spell out numbers (sentence-beginning, <3 digits in ordinary text), when to use figures (groups of six or more tightly connected), and comma usage with thousands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals (Arabic/Roman): spacing and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing of Arabic and Roman numerals at beginning of lines and in headlines; omission of period after numerals, 271, 124.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details typographic spacing conventions for numerals in headings and line beginnings, and punctuation differences for ordinal/other numeral forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates: formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for dates, omission of st/nd/rd/th, comma use between month and year, repetition of hundreds, and placement in bibliographic references, 102, 160, 173, 238.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when to spell out months, omit ordinal suffixes, use commas between month and year, and bibliographic placement of publication dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and measures: capitalization and case
rubrics_metrics.description: Units of measurement spelled with lower-case initial letter; metric symbols and spacing conventions, section references: 55, in, 123c, 269.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies lower-case unit names, metric symbol handling, and spacing rules around measurement symbols and mathematical notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes: numbering, placement, and style
rubrics_metrics.description: General style for footnotes, exceptions, numbering, placing of index figures, and rules for table footnotes, 232–239, 234.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes samples and indexes for footnote references, sequence/numbering conventions, and linotype/monotype considerations for footnote typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and indexing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for indexing: how to number footnote references, placing of index figures, sequence, and alphabetization rules, 232, 236, 240.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes treatment of particles/prefixes in proper nouns, alphabetical ordering of names, and special indexing typographic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and headlines: typography and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and rules for headings, center-heads, box-heads, cut-in-heads, and headlines (capitalization, omission of period, spacing), 279–283, 41, 125, 271.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which words to capitalize in headlines, when to omit terminal periods, and how to format continuation headlines and 'continued' markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: layout, alignment, and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for setting tables, alignment in columns, spacing of figures and decimal points, use of leaders and double rules, and open-table specimens, 241–250, 244–247.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers alignment of numbers and dollar signs, use of leaders for blanks, double rules for table separation, and headline formatting for table heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and illustrations: labeling and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters referring to figures and parts of illustrations, how to set and refer to them in text, 68.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies using italics for letters designating unknown quantities or referring to parts, and placement/formatting of figure references in legends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words (hyphenation and word breaks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and systems for division of words, avoidance of unnecessary division, etymological vs English system, and rules for dividing foreign words, 215–231, 221, 231.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains allowed hyphenation at line end, avoiding division on certain letters, and recommended systems for dividing words by syllable or etymology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation/indention: rules and poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of indentation (indention), rules for hanging indention, indention of poetry, and general indention rules, 274–276, 275, 279, 284.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how to set hanging indents for bibliographies and block quotes, paragraph indention conventions, and special treatment for verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation of clauses (commas, dashes, parentheticals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for punctuation of adverbial, antithetical, appositional, participial, parenthetical, conjunctive, complementary, and summarizing clauses, 144–170.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules for when to use commas or dashes with different clause types, and how punctuation affects clause boundary interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brackets and interpolations: use and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of brackets for interpolations and explanations, and rules for indicating omissions or interpolations, 178.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies bracket use for editorial interpolations, indicating omitted material, and for explanatory insertions in quoted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of en dash vs hyphen: typographic roles
rubrics_metrics.description: En dash defined and its uses (instead of comma between consecutive pages, instead of hyphen in compounds, for 'to' connecting words or figures), 261, 158, 183, 173.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when to use en dash for ranges, in place of hyphen in certain compounds, and spacing/typographic conventions for en dash versus hyphen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Em dash: definition and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Em dash defined and illustrated; use for pauses, omitted words, and 'to' in time-indications, 261, 166–175, 173.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies em dash usage for emphasis, interruption, and substitution for 'to' in ranges of time; includes size/spacing notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing rules: even spacing and hair-spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of even spacing; hair-spacing is tabooed; definitions of em/en spaces and quads, 265, 261, 266.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates consistent interword and punctuation spacing, warns against hair-spacing, and defines typographic space units (em, en, quads).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign words and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on foreign words: italics for foreign-language words, English equivalent to be quoted, division of foreign words, and treatment when incorporated into English, 59, 78, 231.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when to italicize foreign words or supply English equivalents, and how to treat foreign words that have become part of English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of works and publications: italics and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books, pamphlets, essays, poems, periodicals, newspapers, and other works: to be italicized or roman-quoted and rules for capitalization of principal words, 60, 82, 41, 43.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which titles get italics versus roman quotes, capitalization of principal words in titles, and exceptions (e.g., articles not part of newspaper titles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small caps and display typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of small caps, caps, and small caps for specific abbreviations and display elements (A.M., B.C., 'Note' markers), sections 50, 51, 52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates typographic situations where small caps are preferred (certain abbreviations, note headers) and how to indicate capitals in copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bold-face type: definition and indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of bold-face type and how it is indicated, 255.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when bold face is used for emphasis or display and editorial conventions for indicating bold in manuscript copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations like e.g., i.e., cf., ibid., op. cit., loc. cit.: treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Set in roman and spacing conventions for these Latin abbreviations: e.g., i.e., cf., ibid., op. cit., loc. cit., 61, 233.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies roman type for common Latin abbreviations and discusses their bibliographic use and spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetizing and indexing names
rubrics_metrics.description: Alphabetizing rules for names and special treatment of particles/prefixes in proper nouns when indexing, 240.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on ordering names, treatment of 'van', 'de', 'Mac' etc., and conventions for cross-references in indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of plurals and possessives (including numerals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming plurals of irregular or artificial nouns and numerals; rules for possessives and use of apostrophe, 165, 163–165.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes formation of plurals of numerals and special noun forms, and how to form possessives for names and abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of punctuation for emphasis (exclamation, interrogation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for exclamation and interrogation points and their rhetorical uses (doubt, outcry, irony), 127–130.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies conventions for strong emphasis, irony, rhetorical questions, and cautionary use of exclamation points in formal prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists and enumerations: parentheses and subdivision markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of parentheses with letters or figures for subdivisions and enumerations, and formatting of enumerated lists, 176.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses whether to use (a), (1), etc., in enumerations and how to punctuate and indent subdivisions in lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic notes on machine composition (Monotype, Linotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions and typesetting notes for Monotype and Linotype machines, including spacing and special handling of footnotes and proofs, 293–294, 259–260.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance for production staff on setting matter on different typesetting machines and implications for spacing and footnote numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of letters and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set address lines at opening and end of letters, use of commas after address lines, and when to italicize address lines, 50, 64, 161.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains placement of address lines, when to omit commas after addresses, and typographic treatment (italics) for address components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and proof conventions (galley, page, foundry-proof, foul proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and usage for galley-proof, page-proof, foundry-proof, foul proof, and general make-up and folio conventions, 285–288, 290–292.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines proof stages and typesetting deliverables and offers rules for marking and correcting proofs and setting folios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of legal and formal names (acts, laws, bills, courts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization and typography rules for juridical acts, laws, bills, names of judiciary and legislative bodies, 12, 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies capitalization and formatting for legal documents, court titles, and legislative sessions and members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of bibliographic references and periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for bibliographic presentation: volume/page/date ordering, when to italicize journal titles, and footnote formatting for periodicals, 237–239, 60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers symbols for pages, use of italics for periodical titles, punctuation and spacing in references, and sample footnote formats.
